question: During the CDL Vehicle Inspection test, how many vehicle axles will the applicant be required to inspect, though they should be prepared to inspect all axles?
choice_a: One axle
choice_b: All axles on the vehicle
choice_c: Only the steering axle and the rearmost axle
choice_d: Two axles chosen at random by the examiner
explanation: During the test, the applicant will only be required to inspect one vehicle axle; however, they should be prepared to perform the same inspection on all of the vehicle's axles.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection Test, Introduction

question: Committing an 'unsafe act,' such as forgetting to set the parking brake, during the Vehicle Inspection test can result in what?
choice_a: An automatic failure, and the test may be terminated by the examiner
choice_b: A minor point deduction only
choice_c: A verbal warning with no effect on the score
choice_d: No consequence unless it happens twice
explanation: Committing an unsafe act, such as forgetting to set the parking brake, may result in an automatic failure and the test may be terminated by the examiner, since safety is the highest priority.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection Test, Introduction

question: During the CDL Vehicle Inspection test, will an applicant be required to crawl under the vehicle?
choice_a: No, the applicant will not have to crawl under the vehicle
choice_b: Yes, crawling under the vehicle is required for every axle
choice_c: Only if requested by the examiner as a bonus check
choice_d: Only for combination vehicles
explanation: The manual explicitly states the applicant will NOT have to crawl under the vehicle during the CDL Vehicle Inspection test.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection Test, Introduction

question: When entering or exiting the vehicle during the inspection test (other than a bus), how must the applicant safely enter/exit?
choice_a: By facing the vehicle and maintaining three points of contact at all times
choice_b: By facing away from the vehicle for better visibility
choice_c: There is no specific entry/exit procedure required
choice_d: By jumping down from the cab to save time
explanation: When entering/exiting the vehicle, the applicant must safely exit/enter by facing the vehicle and maintaining three points of contact at all times (for a bus, by facing forward and maintaining a firm grasp on the handrail).
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection Test, Introduction

question: During the inspection, what must an applicant do for each safety critical item to receive credit?
choice_a: Name, point to and/or touch, and fully explain to the examiner what they are inspecting each item for
choice_b: Simply point at the item without speaking
choice_c: Write a description on the checklist provided
choice_d: Only touch the item without naming it
explanation: The applicant must name, point to and/or touch, and fully explain to the examiner what they are inspecting each safety critical item for; failing to do so means no credit for that item.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11, Vehicle Inspection Test, Introduction

topic: Iowa Air Brake and Service Brake Check Testing
question: Iowa's CDL Vehicle Inspection test has a distinctive rule for the service brake check step of the inspection. What is it?
choice_a: It should be verbally described only; no physical demonstration is required in Iowa
choice_b: The applicant must physically drive the vehicle at 5 mph and brake in front of the examiner
choice_c: Iowa requires the applicant to disconnect the brake lines to demonstrate the check
choice_d: Iowa exempts CDL applicants from any service brake check
explanation: For the service brake check step (pulling forward at 5 mph and applying the service brake to check for pulling or poor stopping), the manual specifically notes this should be verbally described only, with no physical demonstration required in Iowa.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.1.1, Service Brake Check

question: During the in-vehicle/engine start portion of the inspection, which dashboard indicator lights must be inspected?
choice_a: Turn signal, four-way emergency, high beam headlight, ABS, and DEF/DPF indicators
choice_b: Only the fuel gauge and speedometer
choice_c: Only the check engine light
choice_d: Only the seatbelt reminder light
explanation: The lighting indicators inspection covers dashboard indicator lights for turn signals, the four-way emergency flasher, high beam headlight, Anti-lock Braking System (ABS), and Diesel Exhaust Fluid (DEF)/Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF), if equipped.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.1.1, In-Vehicle/Engine Start, Lighting Indicators

question: What emergency warning devices must be inspected as required emergency equipment inside the vehicle?
choice_a: Three red reflective triangles, six fusee flares, or three liquid burning flares
choice_b: A single fire extinguisher only
choice_c: Two orange safety cones
choice_d: A first aid kit only (school buses excepted)
explanation: The emergency equipment inspection includes checking for three red reflective triangles, six fusee flares, or three liquid burning flares, along with spare electrical fuses (or circuit breakers) and a properly charged and secured fire extinguisher.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.1.1, Emergency Equipment

question: What is the standard for windshield condition during the inspection?
choice_a: It must be clean with no obstructions except an inspection sticker, and no damage such as cracks or flaws
choice_b: Minor cracks are acceptable as long as they don't obstruct the driver's direct line of sight
choice_c: Only cleanliness matters; cracks are not inspected
choice_d: The windshield is not part of the internal inspection
explanation: The windshield must be inspected to be clean with no obstructions except for an inspection sticker, with no damage such as cracks or flaws to the glass.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.1.1, Windshield and Traffic Monitoring Devices

topic: Internal Inspection: Parking and Trailer Brake Check
question: How is the parking brake check performed during the CDL Vehicle Inspection test?
choice_a: With the parking brake engaged, remove the foot from the service brake and gently pull forward to inspect that the parking brake holds the vehicle
choice_b: By driving at highway speed and applying only the parking brake
choice_c: By visually inspecting the brake pads without engaging the brake
choice_d: The parking brake is not tested during the inspection
explanation: For the parking brake check, with the parking brake engaged (and trailer brakes released on combination vehicles, if applicable), the applicant removes their foot from the service brake and inspects that the parking brake holds the vehicle by gently pulling forward.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.1.1, Parking and Trailer Brake Check

question: Failure to explain and demonstrate (perform) how many parts of the air brake check correctly results in an automatic failure of the CDL Vehicle Inspection test?
choice_a: All four parts
choice_b: Any two of six parts
choice_c: Only the final part
choice_d: There is no automatic-failure consequence for the air brake check
explanation: Failure to explain and demonstrate (perform) all four parts of the air brake check correctly will result in an automatic failure of the CDL Vehicle Inspection test.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.1.2, Air Brake Check

question: During the Air Gauge and Governor Cutout Check, at approximately what psi range does the governor cutout typically occur?
choice_a: Approximately 120-140 psi, or the level specified by the manufacturer
choice_b: Approximately 20-45 psi
choice_c: Approximately 55-65 psi
choice_d: Approximately 200-220 psi
explanation: The Air Gauge and Governor Cutout Check involves building air pressure to governor cutout, which occurs at approximately 120-140 psi, or the level specified by the manufacturer.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.1.2, Air Gauge and Governor Cutout Check

question: During the Air Leakage Rate Test on a single vehicle (or trailer without air brakes), how much air pressure drop in one minute is acceptable after the initial stabilization?
choice_a: No more than three pounds in one minute
choice_b: No more than ten pounds in one minute
choice_c: No more than one pound in five minutes
choice_d: Any drop up to 20 psi is acceptable
explanation: After holding the foot brake for one minute, the air pressure should drop no more than three pounds in one minute for a single vehicle or trailer without air brakes, or four pounds in one minute for a combination vehicle.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.1.2, Air Leakage Rate Test

question: During the Air Leakage Rate Test on a combination vehicle, how much air pressure drop in one minute is acceptable after initial stabilization?
choice_a: No more than four pounds in one minute
choice_b: No more than eight pounds in one minute
choice_c: No more than one pound in one minute
choice_d: No leakage is acceptable at all on a combination vehicle
explanation: For a combination vehicle, the air pressure should drop no more than four pounds in one minute after initial stabilization, compared to three pounds for a single vehicle or trailer without air brakes.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.1.2, Air Leakage Rate Test

question: During the Air Warning Device(s) Test, before what air pressure level should the low air warning devices (buzzer, light, and flag) activate?
choice_a: Before air pressure drops below 55 psi
choice_b: Before air pressure drops below 20 psi
choice_c: Before air pressure drops below 100 psi
choice_d: The warning devices are not pressure-triggered
explanation: The low air warning devices (buzzer, light, and flag) should activate before air pressure drops below 55 psi.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.1.2, Air Warning Device(s) Test

question: During the Emergency Brake(s) Test, between what psi range should the parking (or emergency) brake valve pop out?
choice_a: Between 20 psi and 45 psi (no less than 20, no more than 45), or the level specified by the manufacturer
choice_b: Between 55 psi and 65 psi
choice_c: Between 100 psi and 120 psi
choice_d: Exactly at 0 psi
explanation: The parking (or emergency) brake valve should close (pop out) between 20 psi and 45 psi (no less than 20 psi and no more than 45 psi), or the level specified by the manufacturer.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.1.2, Emergency Brake(s) Test

question: On air-operated trailers during the Emergency Brake(s) Test, when should the tractor protection valve and trailer parking brake valve close, relative to the truck/tractor/bus valve?
choice_a: At the same time or prior to the valve for the truck/tractor/bus
choice_b: Always after the truck/tractor/bus valve
choice_c: Only after the vehicle has come to a complete stop
choice_d: There is no required sequence
explanation: On air-operated trailers, the tractor protection valve and trailer parking brake (or emergency brake) valve should close (pop out) at the same time or prior to the valve for the truck/tractor/bus.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.1.2, Emergency Brake(s) Test

question: During the hydraulic brake check, with the transmission in 'park,' how should the brake pedal behave when pumped three times and held down for five seconds?
choice_a: The brake pedal should not move (depress) after initial application and should be firm with sufficient reserve
choice_b: The brake pedal should sink slowly to the floor over the five seconds
choice_c: The brake pedal should feel spongy and depress fully
choice_d: There is no standard for pedal firmness during this check
explanation: During the hydraulic brake check, after pumping the brake pedal three times and holding it down for five seconds, the pedal should not move (depress) after initial application and should be firm with a sufficient amount of reserve for brake pedal application.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.1.2, Hydraulic Brake Check

question: Does failure to explain and demonstrate the hydraulic brake check correctly also result in automatic failure of the CDL Vehicle Inspection test?
choice_a: Yes, it results in an automatic failure, just like the air brake check
choice_b: No, the hydraulic brake check is optional and ungraded
choice_c: Only a partial point deduction applies
choice_d: Hydraulic brakes are exempt from this rule because they are simpler systems
explanation: Failure to explain and demonstrate the hydraulic brake check correctly will result in an automatic failure of the CDL Vehicle Inspection test, the same as the air brake check.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.1.2, Hydraulic Brake Check

question: During the emergency exits inspection on a passenger or school bus vehicle, how many emergency exits must the applicant demonstrate operate smoothly and close securely?
choice_a: At least one
choice_b: All of them without exception
choice_c: None; only a verbal description is required
choice_d: Exactly three
explanation: The applicant must demonstrate that at least one emergency exit operates smoothly, closes securely, and is not damaged, while confirming the exit and warnings work properly and pointing out how all other emergency exits operate.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.2, Emergency Exits

question: What must be inspected regarding passenger seating during a passenger vehicle inspection?
choice_a: No broken seat frames, seat frames firmly attached to the floor, and seat cushions securely attached to the frames
choice_b: Only the seat cushion color and pattern
choice_c: Only whether seat belts are the correct color
choice_d: Passenger seating is not part of the inspection
explanation: The passenger seating inspection requires checking that there are no broken seat frames, that seat frames are firmly attached to the floor, and that seat cushions are attached securely to the seat frames.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.2, Passenger Seating

question: Which student lights must be inspected on both the front and back of a school bus during the inspection?
choice_a: Strobe light (if equipped), alternately flashing amber lights, and alternately flashing red lights
choice_b: Only the headlights
choice_c: Only the brake lights
choice_d: Only the interior dome light
explanation: The student lights inspection covers the strobe light (if equipped), alternately flashing amber lights, and alternately flashing red lights on both the front and back of the school bus, along with their dashboard indicators.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.3, Student Lights (Front and Back)

question: What is the purpose of the safety arm on a school bus, as described in the inspection section?
choice_a: It forces school students to cross well (e.g., 10 feet) away from the front of the school bus in the driver's view
choice_b: It automatically applies the parking brake when extended
choice_c: It prevents the bus doors from opening while in motion
choice_d: It is a backup mirror system
explanation: The safety arm forces school students to cross well (e.g., 10 feet) away from the front of the school bus in the driver's view, while the stop arm warns other drivers that the bus is stopping or stopped.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.3, Stop Arm(s) and Safety Arm

question: What emergency equipment kits must be inspected as present with unbroken seals on a school bus?
choice_a: Emergency first aid kit and body fluid cleanup kit
choice_b: Only a fire extinguisher
choice_c: Only a tool kit
choice_d: A snack kit for delayed routes
explanation: The school bus inspection requires checking that the emergency first aid kit and the body fluid cleanup kit are present and that their seals have not been broken, which may indicate missing items.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.3, First Aid Emergency and Body Fluid Kits

question: During the Lights Operations Check, how must the operation of external lights be inspected?
choice_a: From outside the vehicle, with the applicant directing the examiner to check specific lights
choice_b: Entirely from inside the vehicle by watching the dashboard indicators only
choice_c: External lights are not required to be checked, only internal indicators
choice_d: By using a mirror to see the lights from the driver's seat
explanation: The operation of all external lights must be inspected from outside the vehicle; the applicant may ask the examiner to assist, directing them to the front, sides, and rear of the vehicle while activating the lights from inside.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.4, Lights Operations Check

question: On a combination vehicle, which part of the trailer must be inspected during the lights operations check?
choice_a: Only the rear of the trailer
choice_b: The entire trailer including the underside
choice_c: Only the front-facing marker lights
choice_d: Trailers are exempt from the lights check
explanation: On a combination vehicle, the applicant needs only inspect the rear of the trailer during the lights operations check.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.4, Lights Operations Check

question: Which fluid levels must be checked during the external inspection of the front of the vehicle/engine area?
choice_a: Engine oil, coolant, power steering fluid, and brake fluid (hydraulic brakes only)
choice_b: Only engine oil
choice_c: Only windshield washer fluid
choice_d: Transmission fluid only
explanation: The critical fluid levels inspection covers engine oil, cooling system/coolant, power steering fluid, and brake fluid for vehicles with hydraulic brakes.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.5.1, Critical Fluid Levels

question: What caution does the manual give regarding checking coolant if the engine is hot?
choice_a: Do not remove the radiator cap if the engine is hot
choice_b: Add cold water directly to a hot radiator to cool it quickly
choice_c: There is no special caution for a hot engine
choice_d: Only check coolant levels when the engine is hot
explanation: The manual cautions that if the engine is hot, the driver should not remove the radiator cap.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.5.1, Critical Fluid Levels

question: What could result from worn, cracked, loose, or broken steering parts?
choice_a: Loss of steering, causing the vehicle to wander or experience serious control problems
choice_b: Only a minor increase in fuel consumption
choice_c: A slightly stiffer steering wheel with no safety impact
choice_d: Faster tire wear only, with no control effect
explanation: Worn, cracked, loose, or broken steering parts could result in loss of steering; movement in the linkage can cause the vehicle to wander or experience other serious control problems.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.5.1, Steering System

question: What is the minimum tread depth requirement (measured at major tread grooves containing wear bars) for steering axle tires versus all other tires?
choice_a: 4/32 inch on steering axle tires, 2/32 inch on all other tires
choice_b: 2/32 inch on steering axle tires, 4/32 inch on all other tires
choice_c: 8/32 inch on all tires uniformly
choice_d: There is no minimum tread depth specified
explanation: The minimum tread depth requirement is 4/32 inch on steering axle tires and 2/32 inch on all other tires, inspected with a tread depth gauge at major tread grooves containing wear bars.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.5.2, Tires

question: Will an applicant get credit for tire inflation inspection if they simply kick the tires or use a mallet?
choice_a: No, the applicant must mention the use of a tire pressure gauge
choice_b: Yes, kicking or using a mallet is an approved method
choice_c: Yes, but only for dual tires
choice_d: Credit is given automatically regardless of method
explanation: The applicant will not get credit if they simply kick the tires or use a mallet to inspect for proper inflation; they must mention the use of a tire gauge.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.5.2, Tires

question: Are welding repairs acceptable on a wheel rim during inspection?
choice_a: No, rims cannot have welding repairs
choice_b: Yes, as long as the weld is inspected by a certified mechanic beforehand
choice_c: Yes, welding is the preferred repair method for cracked rims
choice_d: Welding repairs are only disallowed on steering axle rims
explanation: During the rims inspection, the applicant must inspect for damaged, cracked, or bent rims -- rims cannot have welding repairs.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.5.2, Rims

question: What could result from damaged air bags or shock absorbers in the suspension system?
choice_a: Loss of vehicle control or rollover, and affected vehicle handling and stopping distances
choice_b: Only a bumpier ride with no safety consequence
choice_c: Reduced fuel economy only
choice_d: Increased tire lifespan
explanation: Damaged suspension components can lead to loss of vehicle control or rollover; damaged air bags or shocks can affect vehicle handling and stopping distances.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.5.2, Suspension

question: During the suspension inspection, what should the applicant confirm about how the vehicle is sitting?
choice_a: That the vehicle is sitting level, front to rear and side to side
choice_b: That the vehicle is tilted slightly forward for proper drainage
choice_c: Vehicle leveling is not part of the suspension inspection
choice_d: That the vehicle leans slightly to the driver's side
explanation: During the suspension inspection, the applicant should inspect that the vehicle is sitting level, both front to rear and side to side.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.5.2, Suspension

question: Why must light lenses or covers be inspected for cleanliness and damage?
choice_a: Light lenses or covers must be clean and free of damage for the lights to work properly
choice_b: Lenses only affect the vehicle's appearance, not its function
choice_c: Lens condition is checked only for DOT paperwork purposes
choice_d: Lens inspection is optional and not part of the external inspection
explanation: Light lenses or covers must be clean and free of damage for lights to work properly; the inspection checks that they are the proper color, clean, not broken, and not missing.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.5.1, Lenses

topic: External Inspection: Fluid and Air Leaks
question: What might fluid or air leaks indicate that levels alone might not reveal?
choice_a: Component failure in areas that might not be readily inspected, such as the transmission, fuel system, or air compressor
choice_b: Nothing significant; leaks are purely cosmetic
choice_c: Only that the vehicle needs a wash
choice_d: That the vehicle is due for its next oil change
explanation: Fluid loss and air leaks could indicate component failure in areas where levels might not be readily inspected, such as the transmission or fuel systems, or the air compressor and other air components.
source_note: Iowa Commercial Driver's License Manual (National CDL Manual, 2005 Testing System / 2017 Modernized Version, Supplemental Section 11) -- Section 11.5.1, Fluid and Air Leaks
